criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear Australian benefit, users named, function described with bleaching statistics and literature links. No formal goals, objectives or quantified requirements for orbit, revisit, resolution or latency.

evidence.quote: allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events
Australia’s Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt with weekly tasks and source list provided, feasible sequence. Not tailored to reef payload needs, no contingencies or variation provision, no justification of plan against mission concept.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No calculations, orbit parameters, simulations or payload analysis shown. Only background reading and generic STK tutorials claimed, which is not mission-specific technical progress.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Readable with headings and generally clear writing. Figure has no number or caption, formatting inconsistent, references are bare URLs and Useful Links not matched to in-text citations.

evidence.quote: The final report is due on 20/11/20 at 5pm

technical_issues.issue: No quantified mission requirements for spatial/spectral resolution, revisit, coverage of 344400 km2 reef, or latency for near-real-time; water-penetration and atmospheric constraints of colour-based bleaching detection not addressed.
No launch, orbit, COE, communications or deorbit calculations or STK outputs; term AOEs is non-standard and undefined; tutorials do not demonstrate design progress.

overall: Good reef-monitoring rationale with users and sources, workable schedule using STK. Lacks quantified requirements and any real technical results to guide full design.

feedback.summary: You made a good start with a clear reef-monitoring idea benefiting Australia, named users, and a workable weekly plan with sources and STK preparation. To progress, quantify mission requirements and add mission-specific technical analysis to guide your full design.
next_steps: Quantify your Mission Concept & Rationale requirements for resolution, revisit over the reef area, coverage and latency, and address bleaching-detection constraints.
Strengthen your Project Plan & Preliminary Progress Gantt by tailoring tasks to the reef payload, justifying fit to the concept, and adding contingency time.
Generate your mission-specific STK outputs or orbit/communications/deorbit calculations, define AOEs, caption your figure, and match Useful Links to in-text citations.

criteria.C1: You did well in Mission Concept & Rationale to explain Australian benefit for the Great Barrier Reef and name users like marine and conservation scientists to predict bleaching. For Accomplished, add formal goals, objectives and quantified requirements for resolution, revisit over 344400 km2, latency, and link function to user needs with literature.
criteria.C2: You provided a feasible weekly Gantt chart in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress and a Useful Links source list including NOAA bleaching work. For Accomplished, tailor tasks to reef payload needs, explain why the sequence fits your mission concept, and add provision for variations and contingencies with information sources tied to plan.
criteria.C3: You noted completing STK tutorials 1-4 in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, which shows initiative. For Adequate, show minor mission-specific progress with orbit/COE, communications or deorbit calculations or STK outputs for reef coverage, define AOEs, and briefly interpret results.
criteria.C4: You wrote readably with headings in Project Plan & Preliminary Progress. For Accomplished, number and caption your Gantt chart figure, make formatting consistent, and replace bare URLs in Useful Links with properly cited in-text references that match the list.
